title: Parent letter / homework cover note auto-generator
summary: Adds aiGenerateParentLetter() to client/src/lib/ai.ts — takes { worksheet, schoolName, teacherName, weekStarting, parentTone: 'supportive'|'firm'|'informative' } and returns a one-page letter with a 3-bullet 'How parents can help' section grounded in the worksheet's actual learning objective. Reuses the existing curriculum-authority preamble. Surfaces via a new ParentLetterDialog opened from SendToMenu.
motivation: Twinkl parent letters and home-school records are the most-praised primary-school workload-saver in the review corpus. Teachers want a one-click letter that goes home with the homework — not a separate Word document they hand-edit.

in: client/src/lib/ai.ts — extend with aiGenerateParentLetter() (~120 LoC) using the existing structuredSystemSections pattern
client/src/components/ParentLetterDialog.tsx (new, ~120 LoC) — opens from SendToMenu; inline preview; export as a separate PDF page or appended after the main worksheet
client/src/lib/tool-registry.ts — register parent-letter as a SendToMenu target
Targeted vitest: prompt-shape lock + tone-variation invariants (parent-tone='firm' produces stricter language than 'supportive' on the same worksheet input)
out: Automated email-out to parent contacts (deferred to PR-28 — needs MIS roster + transactional email)
Multi-language parent letter (deferred — bilingual MFL revision shell already exists for MFL homework; general-subject multilingual is Phase H scope)

tone_definitions.supportive: Warm, parent-collaborator voice. Frames any 'parents can help' bullet as a positive opportunity. No 'must' / 'should' verbs.
tone_definitions.firm: Direct, expectations-clear voice. Specifies submission deadline. Uses 'we expect' / 'please ensure'. Still respectful.
tone_definitions.informative: Neutral, fact-first voice. Lists the LO + skills practised + how to support without prescribing tone.

acceptance_criteria: Letter contains: school name, week starting, teacher name, worksheet title, 1-paragraph LO summary, 3-bullet 'How parents can help', signature line.
'How parents can help' bullets are grounded in the worksheet's actual learning objective (no generic 'practise reading' filler).
Three tone variants produce distinguishable outputs (Levenshtein distance ≥40% between any two on the same input).
Export pipeline supports both 'separate PDF' and 'appended to main worksheet'.
related: G1 — pupil auto-marking (parent letter can mention 'your child can practise more at /companion/<token>')
